Creativ Digital is looking for a capable experienced freelance developer to help support and improve modern web, mobile and AI\-enabled client products.

This is a flexible, ongoing contractor opportunity for someone who enjoys practical delivery: getting across an existing product, fixing what matters, improving reliability and shipping useful new features.

Why this role?

* Flexible part\-time hours — typically 15–25 hours per week initially
* Remote\-first — with occasional Sydney workshops or client meetings
* Ongoing work across multiple projects, not just one short engagement
* Competitive hourly rates based on capability and experience

* Opportunity to grow into a trusted technical lead / long\-term delivery partner
* Varied work across web apps, mobile apps, SaaS platforms, APIs and cloud infrastructure

* Reviewing and taking over existing web and mobile applications
* Fixing bugs, improving performance and supporting live systems
* Building new product features across frontend, backend and mobile

* Working with AI features, LLM APIs and agent\-assisted development workflows
* Communicating clearly with product owners and Creativ’s delivery team

* 5\+ years’ commercial software\-development experience
* Strong React and modern JavaScript/TypeScript skills
* Experience with React Native and Expo for mobile app development
* Solid Node.js, APIs and PostgreSQL/database experience
* Experience supporting live cloud applications — AWS, Supabase, Cloudflare or similar
* Practical experience with AI development, including Claude, Bedrock, LLM APIs or AI\-enabled features
* A practical, reliable approach to debugging, QA and safe releases
* Ability to work independently and explain technical issues in plain English

Nice to have

* Agency, consulting, freelance or fractional technical\-lead experience
* GitHub Actions, CI/CD, Stripe, Twilio, Sentry or similar tools
* Experience with SaaS, subscription products, customer portals or mobile apps

Engagement details

* Sydney\-based preferred
* Freelance contractor or part\-time arrangement
* Remote\-first, flexible schedule
* Immediate start available
* Please include your hourly rate, availability and links to relevant work

If you’re a experienced developer who wants flexible, meaningful work across real products — with room to build an ongoing relationship — we’d love to hear from you.

description_text:
**Role title: Intern Pharmacist 2027**


**Role type: Max term contract, full time (1 year, until January 2028\)**


**Role grade: Pharmacist (Unregistered)**


**Shift details: Monday to Friday plus ability to work weekends as per roster requirements**


**Department and location: Pharmacy, St Vincent’s Public Hospital, Sydney**


**Salary: $82,253\.78 \+ Super \+ Salary Packaging**

  



**Welcome to St Vincent’s Hospital Sydney**


Join a team built on a proud legacy of world\-class care, true compassion, and deep community roots.


Founded by the Sisters of Charity and powered today by St Vincent’s Health Australia, the Sisters' legacy of compassionate service is our living heartbeat. As Sydney’s premier and iconic inner\-city public hospital, we serve the entire population, providing world\-class care to all people, including the most vulnerable in our community. Across our renowned precinct, we feature cutting\-edge programs and surgery infrastructure, fostering clinical excellence and professional growth.


Located in the vibrant heart of Darlinghurst, we are positioned just minutes from Kings Cross station, with direct, high\-frequency bus connections from the east, and seamless links from Gadigal and Museum stations right to our doorstep.


Read on to explore this exciting role and the fantastic perks waiting for you here.


**About the role**


**Under the supervision of a Pharmacist:**


* Support the delivery of inpatient and outpatient pharmacy services, developing your clinical skills in medication management and pharmaceutical care planning
* Develop your skills in patient counselling, medication education and the provision of drug information to patients, carers and other healthcare professionals
* Gain hands\-on experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing, including the preparation of extemporaneous pharmaceuticals and applying relevant quality and safety controls
* Participate in pharmacy practice research, including undertaking a specific research project
* Work collaboratively within the pharmacy team, participate in weekend rosters and undertake other duties as required by the Director of Pharmacy or Deputy Director of Pharmacy

**About you**


* Successful completion of a Pharmacy Degree and eligible for provisional registration with AHPRA plus eligibility to enrol in an approved Intern Training Program prior to commencement **(You must upload a copy of your academic transcript as part of your application)**
* Sound knowledge of pharmacology and the ability to apply this knowledge in practical clinical situations
* Excellent written and oral communication skills, with demonstrated interpersonal skills and the ability to effectively counsel patients and carers and collaborate with healthcare professionals at all levels
* An understanding of the role of a Hospital Pharmacist, including professional, ethical and legal responsibilities, with a commitment to ongoing professional development, continuing education, quality improvement and research
* A proactive and adaptable team player with demonstrated initiative, strong problem\-solving, time management and prioritisation skills, and the ability to work independently, meet deadlines and contribute effectively within a busy team environment

**What we can offer you**


* **Exceptional Rewards:** Competitive pay and not\-for\-profit salary packaging to maximise your income
* **World\-Class:** Be part of a renowned precinct alongside the Garvan \& Victor Chang institutes
* **Excellence:** Premier heart/lung transplant program, advanced robotics, \& pioneering HIV/AIDS initiatives
* **Cutting\-Edge Oncology:** Deliver advanced cancer care and trials at the renowned Kinghorn Cancer Centre
* **Community:** Support vital programs for First Nations, homelessness, mental health, \& drug and alcohol care
* **Professional Advancement:** Accelerate your career with study leave and Curran Foundation scholarships
* **Health \& Wellbeing:** Fitness Passport, discounted private health, \& cultural recognitions and celebrations
* **Coming from NSW Health?:** Smooth transfer of your qualifying service and leave entitlements

**Sponsorship / work rights for** **Australia**


Please note, visa sponsorship is not available for this position. For this role you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or have an Australia visa that grants you the work rights necessary for the role.


**Equal opportunity**


We celebrate diversity \& inclusion and are committed to equal employment opportunity for everyone.


As part of our commitment to reconciliation, we encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples to apply and join us in delivering care that heals body, mind, spirit and community.


**How to apply**


The closing date for applications is **30th September 2026\.**


Shortlisting for this position will commence immediately. We encourage you to apply promptly as the advertisement may close early should a suitable applicant be sourced.


**Please ensure you upload a copy of your academic transcript as part of your application. Applications without an academic transcript will not be eligible for review.**


Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter highlighting how your interest, skills, and experience align with each of the things listed in the About You section of this job advert.

  


Respectfully, this role is not open to recruitment agencies.

**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

Optimize services and solutions for our global clients across all lines of business. Gain an unparalleled view of our leading financial organization while driving our clients' businesses forward with strategic support and end\-to\-end process management.




**What you Can Expect**




As a trainee in the 2027 Sydney Traineeship Program within JPMorgan Chase, you will participate in a 2\-year full\-time paid program, gaining essential knowledge and skills to build a dynamic, long\-term career with us. You will have the opportunity to work on either the Operations or Finance \& Business Management tracks, optimizing services for global clients or engaging in financial analysis and reporting. You will act as a trusted advisor, ensuring the integrity of financial statements, and contribute to strategic business decisions. You will also complete the nationally recognized qualification Financial Markets Certificate from the Australian Financial Markets Association (AFMA).




Operations


Optimize services and solutions for our global clients across all lines of business. Gain an unparalleled view of our leading financial organization while driving our clients' businesses forward with strategic support and end\-to\-end process management. We're looking for results\-oriented individuals with enthusiasm for developing strategies that optimize business operations.


Finance and Business Management


Finance \& Business Management offers challenging opportunities to work on local regulatory reporting, month end close process and project\-related work on new products/or system implementation. You will get to understand a wide range of different derivative products, the implications of control issues and their potential impact on the legal entity financial statements and regulatory filings. We are looking for highly motivated individuals who have a passion for analysis that will help drive strategic business decisions.


Team allocation will be based on business needs.

**Job responsibilities**

* Act as a trusted advisor to business and group heads by identifying, escalating, and mitigating business risks and optimizing business performance by driving key initiatives.
* Responsible for ensuring the overall integrity and validity of the financial statements and controls over the transaction cycle; performing critical reporting and controls functions for the organization.
* Create meaningful analysis and reporting in support of our businesses. Coordinate with partners across the firm to provide financial and strategic analysis, creation, oversight, and coordination of budgeting and forecasting.
* Contribute to programs that are large scale and comprised of multiple projects and work streams.
* Create effective procedures and support process improvement that are adhered to company standards.
* Ensure timely completion of team tasks and responsibilities.
* Become a key Intelligent Solutions member and work on automation initiatives across the team.
* Actively engage in learning the operational processes within Operations.
* Represent team through a wide array of People initiatives across the organization.




**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills**

* Must be a current Year 12 student and have obtained a high school certificate by the time the program commences
* Must not have commenced or graduated from a degree, Certificate IV qualification, or higher at the time the program commences. **Participation in the Traineeship Program requires full\-time commitment; simultaneous enrollment in other studies is not allowed.**
* Must be Australian citizen or Permanent Resident
* Strong attention to detail
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills
* Comfortable working in teams to deliver results
* Highly motivated with a ‘can\-do' attitude
* Ability to multi\-task and work in a fast\-paced environment
* Available to start work in March 2027




**Application Period:**


August \- November 2026

**Application Deadline:**


20 November 2026 at 12:00noon AEDT


We encourage early applications as screening will be conducted on a rolling basis.

**Program Period:**


March 2027 – March 2029

**What's next?**

* Submit a complete and thoughtful application, which includes your resume. Your application and resume is a way for us to initially get to know you. It's important to complete all relevant application questions, so we have as much information about you as possible. We will review your application to determine whether you meet the required qualifications.
* If you are advanced to the next step of the process, you'll receive an email invitation to complete a video interview within 48hrs, powered by HireVue. This is your opportunity to further bring your resume to life and showcase your experience for our recruiting team and hiring managers.
* HireVue is required, and your application will not be considered for further review until you have completed this step. We strongly encourage that you apply and complete these required elements as soon as possible, since applications will close once positions are filled.




**Note:** This is a paid, full\-time program. Successful applicants must commit full time, simultaneous enrollment in other studies is not allowed. Students planning to attend university may explore our internship opportunities, which are open to penultimate\-year university students, on our Careers website.


For enquiries, please email us at aus.grad@jpmorgan.com


**ABOUT US**
  

  

J.P. Morgan is a global leader in financial services, providing strategic advice and products to the world's most prominent corporations, governments, wealthy individuals and institutional investors. Our first\-class business in a first\-class way approach to serving clients drives everything we do. We strive to build trusted, long\-term partnerships to help our clients achieve their business objectives.

We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. **ABOUT THE TEAM**
  

  

Our professionals in our Corporate Functions cover a diverse range of areas from finance and risk to human resources and marketing. Our corporate teams are an essential part of our company, ensuring that we're setting our businesses, clients, customers and employees up for success.

HKA is one of the world’s leading independent provider of consulting, expert and advisory services working on complex disputes, investigations and commercial matters.

Research into aged care and dementia care is one of the most useful contributions anyone can make to Australian health services today. Reporting to Associate Professor Nasir Wabe, you will contribute to literature reviews, ethics and grant applications, data management and analysis, and the preparation of research outputs for publication and presentation. This is a valuable opportunity for someone early in their research career who would like to build methodological depth alongside a multidisciplinary team of researchers, educators and clinicians. You will be part of a centre of approximately 50 staff, applying research techniques that range from randomised controlled trial designs through to direct observation of clinical work.

**About the Role**


Working under general direction, you will provide practical research assistance across a range of projects within CHSSR. Key responsibilities include:

* Conducting literature searches and preparing bibliographies for use by principal researchers
* Assisting with the conduct of research, primarily in aged care, using a variety of research techniques
* Contributing to the preparation of ethics applications and grant applications to help secure approval and funding for specific projects
* Assisting with the preparation of research data, documentation and reports for presentation and publication
* Assisting with data management and analysis, including computational and statistical analysis
* Undertaking research administrative tasks, such as coordinating project meetings
* Liaising with internal contacts including Macquarie University research and clinical staff and students, and external contacts including researchers at other study sites and aged care providers and clients
* Complying with relevant EEO and WHS requirements
**About Us**


The Centre for Health Systems and Safety Research is one of the core research centres within the Australian Institute of Health Innovation. CHSSR runs a multi\-stream program of research investigating the outcomes and safety of health services, with recognised expertise in assessing the impact of information technologies and the role of electronic health records and decision support in improving health care delivery and health outcomes.


The Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences is expanding the boundaries of progressive thinking and rethinking what's possible in addressing some of the significant issues of our time, both nationally and globally. Here you will join researchers, educators and internationally respected clinicians who are united in a mission to deliver the best patient care. We are a place of original discovery and distinctive educational programs that prepare the future of healthcare.

**About You**

You are methodical, well organised and comfortable handling data and documentation with accuracy, and you communicate clearly with colleagues and external partners. An interest in aged care, dementia care or health services research will serve you well in this role.

**Selection Criteria**

* Demonstrated experience conducting literature reviews, including designing search strategies for online databases such as PubMed. Experience with systematic reviews and meta\-analyses is desirable.
* Demonstrable skills in MS Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), together with experience assisting with data management and analysis, including computational and statistical analysis.
* Sound organisational skills and a high level of attention to detail, including the ability to progress multiple tasks to deadline.

* **Contour Medprep:** Reshaping medical preparation with a proven, step\-by\-step pathway through the UCAT, interviews, and admissions, led by a team of 100\+ medical students.
* **Contour TestPrep:** Reshaping test preparation, starting with the selective entry exam, through rigorous tutoring, mock exams, and data\-driven feedback to give students a decisive advantage.


This is Contour. Built by students, for students.

#### **What You Will Do**


As our State Subject Curriculum Lead, you’ll own the educational source of truth for Chemistry across NSW and strategically direct everything built from it.

* **Map:** Build and maintain the curriculum source of truth for your subject, mapping out NESA syllabuses, recurring exam questions, and common student pitfalls.
* **Pace:** Translate curriculum insights into live topic sequencing, question\-type maps, and school\-specific workshops kept 1\-2 weeks ahead of local classrooms.
* **Support:** Design the targeted materials and support systems students need to conquer internal assessments, optimise their school ranks, and ace the HSC.
* **Direct:** Plan educational resources upstream from the source of truth, briefing and steering Resource Developers so production never bottlenecks on you.
* **Govern:** Act as the final quality gate, signing off on all subject materials with absolute polish while continuously pushing curriculum innovation.

#### **What You Will Bring**

#### **You qualify through either pathway:**

* **As a top graduate:** 98\+ ATAR with a Band 6 in HSC Chemistry. State ranks are ideal, but not compulsory.
* **Or as an experienced teacher:** you have taught HSC Chemistry at a school. If you’ve taught it, you don’t need the ATAR or band requirements above.


And in either case:

* Deep curriculum expertise and strong opinions on how the subject is sequenced, taught, and examined under NESA.
* Excellent documentation skills with a focus on building durable, written educational frameworks.
* Uncompromising attention to detail with an obsession for error\-free work and polished formatting.
* High operational bandwidth to hit tight production deadlines and patch issues proactively.
* Comfort using modern software and AI tooling to accelerate documentation and drafting on top of your own craft (preferred).
* Alignment with Contour’s student\-first mission and a passion for reshaping education.

#### **Why You Will Love It**

* **Reshape How a State Learns:** Your curriculum decisions become the course itself. Every sequencing call, every assessment strategy, every standard you set reaches real classrooms and real students from day one.
* **Founding Role in NSW:** Lead the charge in our newest state with our very first HSC cohort. Create an entire curriculum from the ground up rather than inherit one.
* **Ownership \& Autonomy:** Freedom and trust to run the state’s curriculum your way, working directly with the national Head of Subject. No bureaucracy, no committees.
* **Remote/Hybrid \& Flexible:** Work from wherever suits you, part\-time, on a schedule that fits around your degree, teaching load, or career. We value your output, not the hours you clock.
* **Elite Brand \& Real Benefits:** Join an organisation ranked \#8 on the AFR Fast 100 in 2025 (our fourth consecutive year on the AFR lists), with an EAP, birthday/loyalty leave, lifestyle allowances, and covered subscriptions to Netflix, Spotify, Apple Music, Uber One, and Amazon Prime.
* **Salary:** $100,000 \- $120,000 full\-time equivalent \+ super, pro\-rated to part\-time hours

#### **How to Apply**


If you care about reshaping education and empowering the next generation of students, we'd love to hear from you.

#### **Application Process**

* Submit your written application (CV and study scores)
* Complete a technical assessment using resources we provide
* Attend an interview, which includes Q\&A and a live technical exercise

  

The course you design here is the one a whole state of students will learn from. That’s the bar.

**Lead Faith. Inspire Learning. Shape Futures.**

  

St Andrew’s Cathedral School is seeking a dynamic, creative and theologically grounded Christian educator to join our leadership team as Head of Christian Development.

  

This strategic leadership position is responsible for leading teaching and learning within the Christian Development Department, including oversight of Years 7–12 Christian Development and Stage 6 Studies of Religion.

  

The successful applicant will bring energy, educational imagination and intellectual curiosity to the role. They will inspire students and staff, lead curriculum innovation and promote educational excellence through a distinctly Christian worldview.

  

Located in the heart of Sydney’s CBD, St Andrew’s Cathedral School is a diverse, future\-focused Anglican school committed to academic excellence, educational innovation and the development of young people who lead with hope and purpose.

 **The Opportunity**


Reporting to the School Chaplain and working closely with the School’s Teaching and Learning leadership, the Head of Christian Development will provide educational, theological and organisational leadership for the Department.

  

You will lead the development, implementation, evaluation and continuing renewal of an engaging and coherent Christian Development curriculum. You will help students across the full spectrum of belief—from committed Christians to those who are curious, uncertain or resistant—to encounter the claims of Christianity thoughtfully and respectfully.

 **Key Responsibilities**


As Head of Christian Development, you will:

  

* Lead the development of imaginative, biblically faithful and intellectually rigorous Christian Development programmes.
* Oversee Years 7–12 Christian Development and Stage 6 Studies of Religion.
* Inspire innovative teaching through Scripture, story, inquiry, discussion, debate, philosophy, history, the arts and contemporary culture.
* Foster exemplary teaching practice and support staff growth through coaching, mentoring and professional development.
* Encourage teachers to experiment thoughtfully, share creative practice and continually renew the curriculum.
* Manage departmental planning, assessment, reporting, budgeting, staffing and compliance requirements.
* Use appropriate evidence, including assessment information, student voice and teacher evaluation, to improve teaching and student engagement.
* Build a positive, collaborative and supportive departmental culture.
* Work with School leaders to advance strategic educational priorities.
* Contribute to the wider Christian educational vision of the School and support thoughtful Christian integration across school life.

 **About You**


You are a dynamic and imaginative educator who can bring significant ideas to life. You can make complex biblical, theological and philosophical questions accessible, memorable and compelling for young people.

  

You will demonstrate:

* A vibrant and mature Christian faith lived with integrity.
* Active involvement in a Christian church.
* A collaborative, relational and servant\-hearted leadership style.
* Demonstrated creativity and innovation in curriculum design and classroom practice.
* A proven ability to engage adolescents in questions of faith, ethics, identity, apologetics and worldview.
* Excellent interpersonal, organisational and communication skills.
* The capacity to inspire, coach and develop teachers.
* Professional credibility and a commitment to continual improvement.
* An ability to build positive relationships with students, staff, families and the wider community.

 **Qualifications and Experience**

  

The successful applicant will:

* Hold a recognised degree\-level theological qualification, such as a Bachelor of Theology, Bachelor of Divinity, Master of Divinity or equivalent, including substantial study of Scripture and Christian doctrine.
* Be able to teach and lead consistently with the Anglican evangelical identity of the School, including the doctrine expressed in the Thirty\-nine Articles.
* Hold recognised teaching qualifications and current NESA accreditation.
* Have relevant and successful secondary classroom\-teaching experience.
* Demonstrate experience in curriculum development, educational innovation and the leadership of teaching and learning.
* Understand contemporary educational practice and the effective use of evidence to improve student learning.
* Demonstrate the capacity to lead staff, manage departmental responsibilities and contribute constructively to whole\-school initiatives.
* Have experience teaching Studies of Religion, or the qualifications and capacity to do so.

 **Why Join Us?**


This is an exciting opportunity to shape the future of Christian Development within a distinctive city school. You will lead a dedicated team and help create a programme recognised for its theological substance, intellectual vitality and educational creativity.

  

Applications are invited from suitably qualified Christian educators who are passionate about inspiring curiosity, deepening understanding and leading excellence in Christian teaching and learning.

  

A detailed position description is attached top right\-hand side.

 **Applications close: 9 October 2026**


Interviews will commence as applications are received.

 **See here for further employment benefits at SACS:** https://www.sacs.nsw.edu.au/employment/

 **About St Andrew's Cathedral School**


St Andrew's Cathedral School is an independent Anglican school located in the heart of Sydney's CBD, serving students from Kindergarten to Year 12\. Guided by our vision to develop graduates who "lead with hope as co\-creators of a responsible future", we are committed to an education that combines academic excellence with Christian faith, character formation, service and innovation.

  

Located across two high\-rise buildings in Sydney's CBD, St Andrew's Cathedral School offers a strong academic program alongside extensive opportunities in sport, music, drama and outdoor education. As an authentically Christian school in the Anglican tradition, Christian values are embedded in all aspects of daily life, with honesty, integrity, humility, respect and service forming the foundation of our community.

  

Our students are encouraged to think deeply, critically and creatively, act courageously, and engage meaningfully with the world around them, with hearts that love, minds that grow and lives that give . We seek to nurture young people who will not simply adapt to the future but help shape it for the better.

In support of SACS’ commitment to embedding child safety (Standard 1\), we ensure that our staff are suitable for working with children and young people and that they are supported (Standard 5\).

  

Staff are required to maintain a child safe culture, act in every child’s best interest and to keep them safe from harm, in accordance with the School’s policies and procedures (Standard 10\) which reflect the Child Safe Standards.

  

It is a condition of employment that all new Staff at the School must sign a written statement or complete an electronic acknowledgement that they have read and understand our Child Safe Policy and the Child Safe Codes of Conduct prior to commencing at the School.

  

Prior to employment at the School, this position requires the successful applicant to have a Working with Children Check clearance in accordance with the Child Protection (Working with Children) Act 2012\.

***As the largest paediatric health service in Australia, we care for thousands of children each year, in hospital and at home. Our people are united by compassion, collaboration and excellence in care.***  

  

Clinical Nurse Educator – Children’s Short Stay Unit Are you a passionate Paediatric Nurse who loves developing others and making a difference at the bedside? The Children’s Short Stay Unit (CSSU) is looking for an enthusiastic and experienced Clinical Nurse Educator (CNE) to join our dynamic team and help shape the knowledge, confidence and capability of our nursing workforce. As a CNE in CSSU, you will have the opportunity to combine your passion for Paediatric Nursing and clinical education, supporting nurses at all stages of their careers. You will play a key role in creating engaging learning opportunities, building clinical capability and supporting staff to deliver safe, high\-quality care to children and their families.
  

  

**Why join us?**
  

CSSU is a fast\-paced and varied Paediatric environment caring for up to 32 patients in an inpatient setting. With a broad clinical caseload, no two days are the same. Our patients are predominantly admitted directly from the Emergency Department and generally have a length of stay of up to 72 hours. Our diverse presentations include respiratory conditions such as bronchiolitis, asthma, pneumonia and COVID, as well as common childhood illnesses including fever, poor feeding, UTIs, gastroenteritis, meningitis and seizures. This diversity provides the ideal environment for a CNE to support nurses to continually develop their paediatric assessment, clinical decision\-making and acute care skills.
  

  

You will also be involved in planning and delivering education across the Network including Speciality Transitional Programs, New Graduate Programs and Mandatory Organisation training. This is a permanent full\-time position of three 12\-hour shifts per week, plus one 8\-hour shift per four\-week roster.
  

  

**What you'll be doing**  

  



  

The Clinical Nurse Educator (CNE) will be responsible for the delivery and evaluation of clinical nursing education. The CNE will work in collaboration with the Nursing Unit Manager (NUM) and Nurse Educator (NE) and wider hospital team to develop and implement clinical education relevant to specialities and basic nursing competencies.
  

  

The CNE will work collaboratively to support clinical education to others outside the ward/ unit when required.

* A resume (maximum 5 pages) outlining your experience
  

* Responses to the questions below:

  

* Current Authority to Practice as a Registered Nurse with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA).

  

* Relevant clinical or education post registration qualifications or such education and clinical experience deemed appropriate by the employer

  

* Demonstrated effective clinical teaching skills

  

* Demonstrated commitment to clinical and professional development

  

* Demonstrated advanced written, verbal and interpersonal skills

  

* Knowledge and understanding of NSQHS Standards relating to education

  

* Knowledge of adult learning principles
